newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Red Cross to send flour, corn to N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Red Cross to send flour, corn to N.Korea.

text.p: South Korea's Red Cross plans to send 630 tonnes of flour to impoverished North Korea this week and expects to deliver about 5,000 tonnes of corn soon, a Red Cross spokesman said on Monday.
The flour, donated from South Korean churches, was due to be shipped on Thursday. The corn was expected to be bought in China for delivery either this week or next week, aid officials said.

South Korean religious and civic groups, which have been raising funds to aid North Korea following reports of starving children in the North, planned to send a further 105,000 tonnes of corn in the next few months, they said.
The Red Cross is the only organisation designated by the Seoul government to hand over private-sector aid to the North.
The Stalinist state has been suffering from acute food shortages after its harvest was devastated by two consecutive years of floods.
The U.N. World Food Programme this month more than doubled an appeal for North Korean food aid to $95.5 million from $46.6 million.
The United States has pledged $10 million and South Korea $6 million for the programme's initial appeal. Both countries have said they are considering further contributions.
